questions.prompt: A two-second segment at 4 megabits/s transfers at 2 megabits/s with half a second buffered and no extra overhead. What follows?

options.label: Four seconds to transfer; the half-second buffer cannot bridge that wait under these assumptions.
Two seconds because transfer time always equals media duration.
A CDN hit proves playback cannot stall.

questions.explanation: Segment size 8 megabits divided by payload throughput 2 megabits/s gives 4 seconds. The buffer does not cover that wait.

questions.prompt: A protected Android window produces a blank screenshot. What does that observation establish?

options.label: Capture policy is observed; identify the DRM security level separately before claiming hardware-only decoding.
Every decoded frame on every platform stays entirely in hardware-only memory.
The browser must be limited to 720p.

questions.explanation: FLAG_SECURE capture behavior and MediaDrm software/hardware levels describe different boundaries.

questions.prompt: A key has output restrictions the current device cannot meet. Can the application assume uninterrupted lower-quality playback?

options.label: Inspect the key status and output policy; downscaling is optional and cannot be assumed.
A cached segment automatically removes output restrictions.

questions.explanation: The selected EME Recommendation distinguishes output-restricted/output-downscaled and does not require downscaling.

questions.prompt: An application acknowledges a playback-position update in a cache. What is still needed to promise recovery?

options.label: Define persistence, scoped ordering and recovery, then test the last accepted revision after failure.
The cache name itself proves durable recovery.
Always keep the highest position, even after an intentional backward seek.

questions.explanation: Accepted revision ordering, intentional seeks and declared storage failure/recovery contracts are separate from a lookup acknowledgement.

questions.prompt: A dated provider table says a browser can reach Ultra HD on qualifying Windows devices. What should a reviewer conclude?

options.label: Check the dated platform/browser requirements and actual device configuration; the maximum is conditional.
Every browser on every platform is permanently limited to 720p.
Every installation of that browser always gets Ultra HD.

questions.explanation: The provider table distinguishes platforms and conditional maxima; it is not a measured guarantee for an arbitrary device/title.
